                    ### Question
                    A 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department for right elbow swelling and pain 45 minutes after he fell while playing on the monkey bars during recess. He has been unable to move his right elbow since the fall. Examination shows ecchymosis, swelling, and tenderness of the right elbow; range of motion is limited by pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the right arm is shown. Which of the following is the most likely complication of this patient's injury?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Polymicrobial infection
opb. Absent radial pulse
opc. Impaired extension of the wrist and hand
opd. Avascular necrosis of the humeral head
ope. Adhesive capsulitis

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The 5-year-old boy's presentation of right elbow swelling, pain, and limited range of motion after a fall suggests a possible fracture or dislocation. The most concerning complication in such cases is vascular injury, which can lead to an absent radial pulse. This is particularly relevant in elbow injuries due to the proximity of major blood vessels. While nerve injury could lead to impaired extension of the wrist and hand, it is less common than vascular complications in acute elbow injuries. Avascular necrosis of the humeral head is a potential risk but is more associated with specific types of fractures, particularly in older patients or those with certain risk factors. Adhesive capsulitis is unlikely to develop acutely following an injury. Therefore, the most likely complication of this patient's injury is an absent radial pulse due to vascular compromise.
